items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> DeepSeek Bot来了！民间版，DSH装个插件就能用 鱼羊 2026-10-11 11:27:08 来源： 量子位 Grok Bot我养不起，ds bot不得高低尝尝咸淡？ 鱼羊 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号QbitAI DeepSeek官方Muse还没来，民间高手们已经迫不及待了。 刚刚新鲜上桌的是「DeepSeek-Bot」： 基于DeepSeek Harness的机器人团队 。 △图源：作者@Fei2411 跟Grok Bot一样，ds bot基于DeepSeek Harness做了一套多Bot团队界面。 每个Bot都可以拥有自己的名字、角色、模型，更重要的是「持久化」——能够积累长期记忆。 另外，为了节省token，你还可以给Bot们安排一个主管，有事先找主管，再让它去协同Bot们就行。 作者FeiZ还给划了重点： 你可以为ds bot接入任何你想接入的模型。未来甚至可以接入本地Agent。 ds bot继承了dsh的「一切皆插件」理念，以保持可拓展性。 虽然非官方，不过似乎这才是蓝色大肥鱼的正统风味（bushi）？ 上线不到一天，大肥鱼爱好者们已经给这个项目点了250+星。 Grok Bot我养不起，ds bot那不得高低尝尝咸淡？ 基于DSH的bot插件 一切皆插件，ds bot同样是插件的形式。 主要功能如下。 有问题，先找Bot主管 在ds bot里，每个Bot都有独立身份，可以设置名称、职责说明、指令、形象，以及背后调用的模型。 Bot们具有持久化的运行状态，拥有长期记忆。 还可以设置Main Bot。这个Bot主管拥有高权限，能帮你管理、配置其他Bot和群聊，既能降低管理多个Agent的复杂度，也能在群聊这种狂烧token的环境里，降低token消耗。 这方面，ds bot是专门做了优化的：在一个群聊里设置管理员，你的消息默认会由管理员回复，它会帮你调用其他bot。 当然，你也可以直接@需要单独沟通的bot，来进行一对一。 △图源：作者@Fei2411 总之，作者强烈建议，直接通过和Bot对话来配置其他Bot和群聊。 BTW，作者还提到，Bot的模型可以随时切换。不过： 我仍然建议你长期使用同一个模型，仅在真正需要时才进行切换。 长期记忆 长期记忆是ds bot的一个重点。记忆可以在详情页中管理，也可以直接对话管理。 从技术上来说，每个Bot在底层对应一个DeepSeek Harness Session，拥有自己的工作上下文。 遇到超出上下文窗口的长对话，ds bot会使用压缩、交接摘要和本地搜索等机制管理上下文。 ds bot还为每个Bot设置了基于Markdown文件的记忆存储，同时设计了团队共享记忆。 另外，每轮对话结束后，模型都会进行自动记忆审查，判断哪些信息需要保存、更新或删除。 其他的技术特点还包括： 使用量统计：在Settings → Usage中，可以查看按时间、Bot和模型分类的Token使用情况。 数据本地化：所有数据都保存在你电脑DSH主文件夹目录下的bot/ 和sessions/ 文件夹中。卸载插件不会删除这些数据。 开源与许可：项目采用Apache License 2.0许可。 安装与使用 DSH的桌面端和Web端都能使用ds bot。 桌面端，在侧边栏选择「插件」→「添加插件」，输入「ds-bot」即可安装。 Web端，需要Node.js 22.19或更高版本，以及pnpm。然后通过以下命令来添加插件： npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-alpha.1 plugin –profile web add ds-bot npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-alpha.1 web 更多细节，可以参见项目主页。 那么，如果你感兴趣，就可以耍起来了，欢迎回到评论区留下你的使用反馈呀~ 项目地址： https://github.com/FeiZhuLulu/DeepSeek-Bot/tree/main — 完 — 版权所有，未经授权不得以任何形式转载及使用，违者必究。

Now, we’re partnering with game developers to prototype new gameplay experiences that push the frontiers of both gaming and AI. Since DeepMind’s foundation in 2010, the constrained yet rich worlds of games have played a critical role in understanding intelligence. They have driven some of our biggest AI breakthroughs, from mastering Atari to helping solve protein structure prediction - and they are still at the heart of what we do. Gaming is in GDM’s DNA. Demis Hassabis, one of Google DeepMind's founders, is himself a former game developer, as are many of us in the GDM team. Together, we have decades of hands-on experience in game development and a deep respect for the craft of making games. We’ve always been clear that doing AI research with games requires deep partnership with game developers - like our major new research partnership with Fenris Creations and the EVE Universe that we unveiled earlier this year, and the work we’ve done together with acclaimed studios like Hello Games , Coffee Stain Studios , Foulball Hangover and others. Games as the engine of AI research Our journey began when a small team trained a deep neural network to play Atari 2600 games directly from raw pixels. The Deep Q-Network (DQN) learned to play 49 different games — from Pong to Breakout to Space Invaders — without any game-specific engineering. The 2015 Nature paper on DQN helped catalyze the modern era of deep reinforcement learning. From there, we attempted to master more complex games, with each milestone producing more capable and general systems. items.full_text_snippet: For robots to assist humans in everyday environments, accurate spatial reasoning is not enough. Robots must also think fast, timing their decisions and reasoning with the real-time speed of the physical world. That’s why today we’re launching Gemini Robotics ER 2 , our most capable “embodied reasoning” model for robotics. Think of Gemini Robotics ER 2 as a high-level brain for robots. It allows robots to chat with humans, understand the physical world, and plan multi-step tasks. It then hands off motor execution to any given lower level vision-language-action (VLA) model. Gemini Robotics ER 2 can also natively call tools like Google Search to find information, or any other user-defined function. The design of Gemini Robotics ER 2 allows the robot to “think” about what comes next while simultaneously performing its actions. Gemini Robotics ER 2 represents a significant upgrade over Gemini Robotics ER 1.6 . By watching continuous video feeds, robots can now track their own progress, adapt if something goes wrong, and know exactly when to move on to the next step. We are also introducing multi-robot collaboration, enabling robots to work together in shared spaces and complete complex workflows a single robot could not do alone. Gemini Robotics ER 2 is now publicly available to developers via the Gemini API , Google AI Studio , and in private preview on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform . To help you get started, we’re sharing examples of how to configure the model and prompt it to power more useful physical AI tasks. Advancing physical agentic capabilities Most tasks in the physical world are complex and require multiple steps to complete. Gemini Robotics ER 2 is a physical agent, orchestrating steps for the robot and enabling it to self-correct, and generalize to more novel situations. items.full_text_snippet: Long agent traces composed of chains of thought and tool calls accumulate stale content that anchor subsequent generations, and eventually outgrow the context window. Existing scaffolds mitigate it with fixed-interval compaction triggered at a token threshold. Such triggers pay no heed to trajectory structure, risking discard of partial results mid-derivation or mid-search.  We propose SELFCOMPACT, a scaffold that allows the model itself to decide when and how to compact. Specifically, it pairs two inference-time elements: (i) a compaction tool the model invokes to summarize the accumulated context, and (ii) a lightweight rubric specifying when to fire (a sub-task has resolved, or the trajectory is converging) and when to suppress (mid-derivation, or when stuck). Both are needed. The tool alone is unevenly used across open-weight models, often invoked at unhelpful moments or not at all; the rubric alone cannot act. Together, they elicit effective adaptive compaction without any fine-tuning or external supervision. We present empirical results on six benchmarks (competitive math and agentic search) and seven models. Our results show that SELFCOMPACT matches or exceeds fixed-interval summarization at a fraction of the token cost, improving over a no-summarization baseline by up to 18.1 points on math and 5–9 points on agentic search at 30–70% lower per-question cost. Our results expose a meta-cognitive gap: although unprompted models cannot reliably tell when their own context is rotting, a lightweight rubric closes this gap, reframing when to compact as a capability that scaffolds can supply without training. † Johns Hopkins University

items.full_text_snippet: DeepSeek AI, a prominent player in the large language model arena, has recently published a research paper detailing a new technique aimed at enhancing the scalability of general reward models (GRMs) during the inference phase. Simultaneously, the company has hinted at the imminent arrival of its next-generation model, R2, building anticipation within the AI community. The paper, titled “ Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling ” introduces a novel method that allows GRMs to optimize reward generation by dynamically producing principles and critiques. This is achieved through rejection fine-tuning and rule-based online reinforcement learning [1-1]. This development comes at a time when the paradigm for scaling LLMs is shifting from the pre-training stage to post-training, particularly the inference phase, following the emergence of models like OpenAI’s o1. This approach leverages increased reinforcement learning (computational effort during training) and more extensive “thinking time” (computational effort during testing) to continually improve model performance. Notably, o1 generates a lengthy internal chain of thought before responding to users, refining its reasoning process, exploring different strategies, and identifying its own errors. DeepSeek’s own R1 series of models has further validated the potential of pure reinforcement learning training (without relying on supervised fine-tuning) to achieve significant leaps in LLM reasoning capabilities. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 8 Oct 2026] Title: Leakage-Resistant Evaluation of AI-Generated Database Specifications in Specification-Driven Migration View a PDF of the paper titled Leakage-Resistant Evaluation of AI-Generated Database Specifications in Specification-Driven Migration, by Oleg Grynets and 2 other authors View PDF Abstract: This paper presents a leakage-resistant framework and benchmark (LRFB) for measuring evaluators of AI-generated Oracle PL/SQL specifications. The benchmark contains 494 labelled source-specification pairs across 19 quality metrics grouped into seven dimensions; each metric contains 26 records divided into development and held-out subsets of 13 records each, with three clean and ten defective specifications per subset. Ground truth is mechanically sealed from inference and checked with canary and label-permutation tests. Three LLM judges were evaluated with three runs per record and compared against two trivial baselines. On 247 held-out records, GPT-4o, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 reached balanced accuracies of 0.87, 0.89, and 0.81, respectively, while a specification-length baseline reached 0.88. Exact paired tests did not separate any judge from that baseline. The judges nevertheless provided information unavailable to length: the labelled defect category appeared among findings in 84%-92% of violated records, and quoted evidence overlapped the labelled span in 92%-93%. The study therefore reframes specification evaluation from binary issue detection toward evidence-linked, typed findings and benchmark-validity controls. items.full_text_snippet: The increasing demand for GPU-accelerated machine learning inference has exposed limitations in centralized GPU infrastructures, including high cost, limited elasticity, and long wait times under resource constraints. At the same time, modern Apple Silicon–based macOS devices are equipped with powerful GPUs that remain largely idle during normal usage. This paper presents Minions, a dynamic and distributed virtual GPU cloud that aggregates idle Apple Silicon GPUs across macOS devices to execute large-scale machine learning inference workloads. Minions enables teams to leverage existing hardware without requiring additional GPU procurement. The system provides flexible GPU inference task execution, fault tolerance, and efficient resource utilization. Our experience shows that idle macOS devices can be transformed into a practical distributed GPU inference platform in environments where centralized GPU resources are constrained.

items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 9 Oct 2026] Title: BT-Agent: Deploying Onboard Robot Agents with Behavior Trees and Multi-Fidelity Evaluation View a PDF of the paper titled BT-Agent: Deploying Onboard Robot Agents with Behavior Trees and Multi-Fidelity Evaluation, by Fabio H\"ubel and 7 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Deploying language-model agents onboard mobile robots requires task reasoning and responsive execution within limited compute and memory. We propose BT-Agent, an onboard architecture combining LLM-driven task decisions with predefined behavior-tree (BT) skills. These skills enforce execution conditions and return structured failure feedback. We demonstrate fully onboard operation with a 9B model on a quadruped across five task categories. Intervention tests show that local checks stop ongoing navigation without waiting for another model decision, while the agent remains active to retry or report constraints. To compare agent designs efficiently, we introduce a 161-task multi-fidelity benchmark, evaluated in text on all tasks and in Habitat on 39. Text supports 10.9$\times$ higher evaluation throughput, while simulation reveals how perception and motion failures change task outcomes. BT-Agent's largest success gains over the strongest Act/ReAct baseline occur at 4B and 9B: approximately 10 and 5 percentage points. Ablations identify structured tool calls and informative failure feedback as the most useful components. items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 华为AI靠RSI通关25款游戏！操作次数比人类少56% 一水 2026-10-12 13:48:36 来源： 量子位 一水 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI 一边打游戏，一边给自己升级？ 好家伙，华为这波直接让AI学会了《边玩边变强》啊？！ 最新一项研究，华为诺亚方舟实验室联合UCL等团队拿出了一个名叫 Memento 3 的AI智能体系统—— 直接把ARC-AGI-3公开集里的25款游戏、183个关卡，全部打通了。 还不是靠无脑试错硬闯过去的。 人类完成同样一套关卡，需要17135次操作。 而Memento 3只用了7518次， 比人类少操作约56%，最终拿下了满分100的RHAE成绩 （Relative Human Action Efficiency，相对人类行动效率）。 更离谱的是， 这套系统以Claude Opus 5为底模，全程没有更新模型权重，也没有针对游戏进行微调 。 它就这么自己上手玩，自己琢磨规则，自己写代码，玩错了还会反思、修改。 然后就……满分通关了。 作为对比，Claude Opus 5在ARC Prize官方标准测试框架下，平均RHAE只有约40.7分。 同样的底模，换了套智能体系统，成绩居然直接飙升了59.3分。 还没完。 这套方法不光能玩解谜游戏，研究团队还让它跑去打了Atari经典游戏Pong（乒乓球）。 结果，AI自己摸索出控制策略，随后不用再向大模型请求推理，就连续三局把对手打成了21：0。 不是，大模型都不参与后续操作了，游戏居然还能打得这么溜？！ 关键就藏在这项研究的题目里： Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement，基于世界模型的递归自我改进 。 华为AI直接通关25款游戏，操作次数比人类还少56% 先说说这25款游戏到底什么来头。 它们来自ARC Prize推出的ARC-AGI-3，关注AI评测的朋友，对ARC系列应该不陌生。 但这一代有个非常明显的变化： 不再只是出题解题那一套了，这次是直接把AI扔进陌生的游戏世界 。 规则，是需要AI自己猜的；目标，是需要AI自己找的；操作会产生什么效果，是需要AI自己试的。 AI：合着全都靠我呗~ 这25款公开游戏一共包含183个关卡，画面大多由简单的像素、方块、颜色和图形组成。 乍一看，甚至有点像几十年前的小游戏合集。 但可别被这朴素的画风骗了。 对AI来说，怎么操作不是最难的，最麻烦的是压根不知道这个世界怎么运转。 踩上特殊地板会发生什么？一扇门打不开，是颜色没对上，还是形状不匹配？ 更麻烦的是，后面的关卡还可能出现新规则，把之前摸索出的经验全部推翻。 别说AI了，人类玩家也会卡住 。 ARC Prize的测试数据显示，在一款需要操控变形虫移动、变色的益智游戏r11l中，10名参与者全部通关；而另一款考验符号破译能力的解谜游戏tr87，12人挑战，只有6人成功。 在华为AI之前，各路研究团队就已经卷得相当激烈了： 普林斯顿大学推出的Continual Harness只通关了3款游戏，拿下20.5分。 英伟达研究人员参与开发的DreamTeam稍好一些，通关6款，得分38.1。 再往上，独立研究者David Courtis开发的OPINE-World，以及英伟达团队的NOOA，分别拿到了78.4分和85.1分。 最猛的是独立开发者Sergey Rodionov的baseline1，不仅把25款游戏全部打通，还拿到了99分，距离满分只差1分。 但华为团队这次，直接把最后这1分也补上了 。 Memento 3不仅以100分的成绩通关全部25款游戏、183个关卡，还把总操作次数压到了7518次，比baseline1的8347次又少了829次。 不光通关了，而且还用更少的步骤通关。 怎么做到的？？ 不用训练大模型，AI靠给自己写攻略实现“打怪升级” 翻了下论文，Memento 3的核心方法叫 Code as Model（代码即模型） 。 听着有点抽象，其实就是让AI在玩游戏的过程中，给自己准备两样东西： 一本不断更新的游戏攻略，以及一套能模拟游戏运行的代码。 Rulebook（规则手册）：一份Markdown文档，记录AI在游戏里摸索出的规律，比如什么操作会触发什么效果、怎样才能通关，还有哪些规则没搞明白。 Executable World Model（可执行世界模型）：AI会把自己总结出的规则，直接写成能够运行的Python代码，相当于自己搓了一个简化版的游戏模拟器。...

items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 何恺明团队发布多模态Harness框架 henry 2026-10-11 16:59:06 来源： 量子位 henry 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI 多模态模型的视觉原生Harness，来了！ 最近，何恺明团队在最新论文《VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World》中，提出了一套视觉原生的Harness—— VISTA 。 它让现有的多模态模型直接观察环境、保存原始画面，并在推理时随时回看、放大和检查细节，无需从头训练。 相比于传统将环境抽象成文字或代码的做法，VISTA保留了 原始的视觉信息 。模型可以根据眼下的问题，将过去看过的画面重新调入上下文，参与当前的判断与推理。 基于这套方法，视觉经验成为了模型随时调用、反复检查的上下文，而多模态模型，也有了围绕视觉记忆搭建的原生脚手架。 在评测方面，搭配VISTA，Claude Opus 5.0完成了ARC-AGI-3全部25个公开游戏，相对人类动作效率得分达到满分 100 ，所用游戏动作数比首次游玩的人类基线少 57.4% 。 换成GPT-5.6 Sol，同样全部通关，得分达到99。 更进一步，团队还在浏览器游戏、迷宫和连线题中验证了这套方法，并将更接近物理世界的具身任务列为后续研究方向。 这是怎么做到的？ 视觉原生的脚手架 从ResNet、Mask R-CNN到MAE，视觉感知与表征学习始终是何恺明研究的一条主线。 这一次，VISTA将目光投向了一个新问题：如何让模型在持续交互中积累、保存并利用视觉经验？ 答案是 Harness 。 去年11月，Anthropic曾以长时间编程任务为例，介绍了Harness如何帮助模型跨越多个上下文窗口，持续推进任务。 具体来说，Harness会通过任务清单记录尚未完成的事项，通过进度文件和代码记录保存已经完成的工作。 这样一来，即使模型进入新的上下文窗口，也能通过读取这些信息，了解此前做了什么、接下来该做什么。 复杂任务由此可以分步执行、检查结果，并在不同上下文窗口之间接续工作。 可以说，这套主要通过文字和代码来保存任务状态的Harness，在一定程度上推动了这一波Agent能力的爆发。 然而，在现实环境里， 光有文字记忆，显然还不够 。 因为一旦进入真实的视觉环境，模型不仅需要记住物体的位置、朝向，还要理解每次动作前后，环境究竟发生了哪些变化。 而且 模型第一次看到一张图时，未必知道哪个细节会在后面变得重要。 与此同时，这些视觉信息，也很难提前用一份文字笔记完整记录下来，更难保证模型后续执行任务时，记录的信息依然够用。 在ARC-AGI-3这样的基准中，一种已有思路是先把画面转换成由数字组成的文本网格，再让模型编写程序，模拟环境规则、验证行动方案。 （注释：ARC-AGI-3是一套交互式视觉推理基准，不预先提供游戏规则和目标，智能体需要通过观察和行动，自行摸索如何通关） 但问题在于，环境越复杂，物体的外观、空间关系和动态变化就越难被完整地转化成文字和代码。而且随着交互历史越来越长，早期画面也会被逐渐移出上下文，或者被文字摘要替代。 于是，在这里，VISTA的研究问题就变成了： 如何在不额外训练基础模型的情况下，让智能体在推理需要时，重新检查过去看到的视觉信息？ 基于此，VISTA把 环境返回的每一帧原样存到上下文之外，包括动作过程中的动画中间帧，模型需要时再取回来。 在ARC-AGI-3评测中，它既能比较不同时刻的画面，也能放大局部，检查小方块上的朝向标记。 其中，文字笔记记录模型当前的理解，原始画面保留供它重新判断的证据。 研究将这种机制称为对交互历史的显式注意力，模型根据正在思考的问题，选择哪些视觉信息重新进入上下文。 要想让这种选择成为可能，系统就得保存原始画面，并提供随时调取和检查的工具。 具体实现 为了让模型能够保存并利用过去的视觉经验，VISTA设计了三个核心组件： 视觉观测、无损视觉记忆和主动视觉检查。这三个组件各有分工，分别负责让模型看清画面、保存历史，以及按需回看。 首先是视觉观测，负责将环境画面提供给模型。 items.full_text_snippet: The remarkable success of OpenAI’s o1 series and DeepSeek-R1 has unequivocally demonstrated the power of large-scale reinforcement learning (RL) in eliciting sophisticated reasoning behaviors and significantly enhancing the capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, the core training methodologies behind these groundbreaking reasoning models often remain veiled in their technical reports. Recent community efforts have predominantly focused on mathematical reasoning, leaving the challenge of cross-domain generalization largely unexplored. Furthermore, standard Reinforcement Learning from Preference Optimization (GRPO) training is plagued by common issues such as performance bottlenecks, inefficient sample utilization, and difficulties in cultivating specialized reasoning skills when dealing with mixed-domain datasets. These challenges complicate the effective scaling of RL methods for LLMs. Addressing these limitations, researchers from the Kwaipilot team at Kuaishou have introduced a novel reinforcement learning framework: Two-Staged history-Resampling Policy Optimization (SRPO) . This innovative approach is designed to systematically tackle the aforementioned training challenges across multiple dimensions. The team has publicly released a technical report detailing the intricacies of their training method and has also open-sourced the SRPO-Qwen-32B model. Notably, this work marks the first instance of achieving DeepSeek-R1-Zero-level performance concurrently in both mathematical and code domains . By leveraging the same base model as DeepSeek (Qwen2.5-32B) and employing a purely reinforcement learning training approach, SRPO has achieved impressive results on the AIME24 (50) and LiveCodeBench (41.6) benchmarks, surpassing the performance of DeepSeek-R1-Zero-32B. 来源： 量子位 henry 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI 我真求你们了，论文都多得看不过来了，怎么自动写论文的工具还在往外冒！ 最近，GitHub又又又又上新了一个AI论文生成工具—— Open Academic Paper Gen 。 先别急着划走！ 除了能自动生成一版带参考文献的初稿以外，Open Academic Paper Gen还有个你必须关注的点—— 在能获取文献全文的情况下，它会从 全文 （划重点）中寻找依据，核验论文里的引用观点。 有一说一，这非常实用了。 因为论文写作很多时候，就是从一个研究主题出发，不断梳理观点、寻找证据，再根据文献调整自己的判断。 有了AI之后，论点可以帮你发散，论据也可以帮你检索来源。 但问题在于，有时候观点、论文是真的，可一旦把（AI给的）“观点”放回全文里，结合上下文语境去看，就会发现，作者可能压根不是那个意思。 所以，为了解决这个问题，Open Academic Paper Gen在拿到文献全文之后，会进一步定位相关段落，判断这篇文献到底能不能支撑对应观点。 如果有页码信息，它还会在注释里标出对应的PDF页码，方便人再回去翻查。 也就是说，它不光会查“这篇论文存不存在”，还会查“这话到底是不是它说的”。 一套生成论文初稿的多智能体工作流 总体来看，Open Academic Paper Gen是一套生成论文初稿的多智能体工作流，把从选题到导出的过程，拆成了九个阶段： 确定研究范围、检索文献、清理筛选、分析趋势、寻找切入点、列提纲、写作、核验，最后导出。 和其他AI论文写作工具类似，你给它一个研究主题，比如“物理世界的RSI”。 它就会从这个主题中拆出具体的研究问题，再生成对应的中英文关键词，去OpenAlex、Crossref、Semantic Scholar和arXiv里搜索论文。 搜回来的文献会进一步去重、评分，再由模型筛选相关性。遇到相关性较高的论文，还会顺着它的参考文献，以及后来引用它的研究继续找。 相当于抓住一篇，再顺藤摸瓜补一批，思路其实有点像当年的CONNCTED PAPERS。 （有没有懂的）。 接下来，收集到的文献，会被整理成一张证据表，汇总每篇论文的研究问题、方法、数据、结论以及局限。 有了这些材料，系统再分析研究趋势，提出可能的研究角度、研究空白和假设。 这里还有个挺有意思的环节，叫 创新性诊断 。 Open Academic Paper Gen会从问题、方法、数据和视角几个维度评估切入点，指出文献池中最接近的已有工作，并给出审稿人可能提出的质疑。 （这相当于是在你觉得自己做出ResNet时，AI先帮你看看别人是不是做过） items.full_text_snippet: 平台：Android 关键词：模拟器、Steam、PC、掌机 @大大大K ：最近在 Steam 里买了新游戏玩到上头，上班摸鱼、吃饭等上菜时都想随时随地搓两把。 虽然搭建一个串流很简单，但家里的电脑也不能 24 小时开机，我甚至为此萌生了买一个 Steam Deck 的念头——但就在这个时候，GitHub 推送给我一个开源项目 DroidDeck，它解了我的燃眉之急。 DroidDeck 的运行原理是在 Android 系统中搭建一套 Linux 环境，在这个环境中以大屏模式运行 Steam Linux 客户端，并激活专为 Steam Deck 准备的「Jupiter UI」界面。同时它也能够加载 Proton 转译环境运行 Windows 游戏。 从原理上可以看出，DroidDeck 所需要占用的空间应该不小，根据项目介绍，Linux 环境大概需要 3 GB，Steam 客户端和 Proton 环境所需空间 1.1 GB 左右，这些环境还需要解压安装。 经过实测，在安装了一个 1.5 GB 左右的游戏之后，整个 DroidDeck 所占用的存储空间已经来到了近 12 GB，赶得上一个「小而美」了。另外，因为涉及到图形计算相关的功能，DroidDeck 要求设备支持高通 Adreno 730 或更高规格 GPU 并且运行 Android 9 以上版本，也就是说最早支持到第一代骁龙 8，2021 年或者 2022 年初之后的旗舰、次旗舰设备基本上都能运行。 虽然原理听起来比较复杂，DroidDeck 的易用性还是非常出色的。初次打开 app 会引导你下载并配置好运行环境，然后去开发者选项中关闭子进程限制。点击运行后，DroidDeck 还需要一点时间安装 Steam 客户端和依赖，在屏幕中看到原汁原味的 Steam 大屏模式，你就能登录 Steam 了。期间我们完全不需要去调整各种参数，只需要闭眼点击下一步就可以。 进入 Steam 界面后，我们可以通过触摸进行各种操作，DroidDeck 也会叠加一层虚拟按键模拟 Steam Deck 的物理按键，操作手机返回键时则会触发 DroidDeck 的侧边栏。对小屏设备来说，这层虚拟按键反而会让触摸操作不太方便，我们可以点击左下角按钮隐藏。当然了，如果你有 Android 平板设备或者折叠屏手机，使用 DroidDeck 的体验会更棒。 Steam Linux 客户端中已经内置了官方的 Proton 转译环境，支持的游戏可以直接运行。DroidDeck 还提供了额外的 2 个 ARM64 Proton 构建版本，如果某个游戏体验不佳，或许切换 Proton 版本能够解决。需要注意的是，由于是转译运行，所以并不是所有游戏都能支持，我们可以在每个游戏的兼容性支持信息中查看到具体兼容情况。就我个人实际使用体验来看，一些性能要求不高的游戏运行起来毫无压力，帧率稳定、响应快速，3A 游戏体验会差一些。 除了 Steam 游戏库之外，DroidDeck 也支持通过插件工具整合 GOG、Epic Games 平台，接入后同样可以使用 Proton 启动游戏（巫师三启动！），不过这一点可能需要折腾一下。此外我们还能在 DroidDeck 设置中打开 Linux 桌面并安装常用的工具和模拟器（比如 PPSSPP 等），进一步丰富了可玩性。 DroidDeck 本身的使用体验也非常可圈可点，UI 设计美观、操作动画流畅、界面逻辑清晰，不失为一个优秀的产品案例。如果你手头恰好有一台专门的高性能 Android 游戏掌机或大屏设备，也想获得与 Steam Deck 相似的随身游戏体验，可以前往 GitHub 下载尝鲜。

items.full_text_snippet: 2026 年 6 月，Apple 在 WWDC26 上预览了 iOS 27、iPadOS 27 等系统，并公布了一系列新的家长控制与儿童安全功能，相关功能随后随 9 月的软件更新正式推出。使用新版家长控制功能，需要「家人共享」群组内的设备都升级到 iOS 27、iPadOS 27、macOS 27、watchOS 27 或 visionOS 27，并由组织者或家长更新家长控制设置。否则只能继续使用旧版功能或直接在儿童设备上调整。 此次升级的核心集中在内容限制、通信安全、浏览请求、时间限制等几个方面。Apple 还将原有的「屏幕使用时间」重新设计，并进一步把家长控制前置到儿童账户的初始设置中。 儿童账户可以在首次设置时直接配置 OS 27 增加了更完整的儿童账户设置流程，儿童账户的年龄界限因国家或地区而异。在中国大陆，未满 14 周岁的儿童需要由父母或监护人协助创建 Apple 账户；儿童账户可一直使用至 18 周岁。现在，Apple 账户按照用户的年龄段分为以下三类： 儿童：13 岁及以下 青少年：14-17 岁 成人：年满 18 岁 对于青少年和儿童账户，在配置儿童使用的新设备时，家长可以直接设置将青少年和儿童账户连接至家人共享。整个连接流程与首次配置 Apple Watch 和 HomePod 很像，使用家长的设备扫描动画，即可将儿童的设备加入到家人共享。 需要注意的是，家长必须证明自己是成年人，才能为儿童创建 Apple 账户。在中国大陆，家长必须在自己的 Apple 账户的付款方式里添加信用卡（借记卡、支付宝等均不符合条件）；在其它部分地区，还可以通过扫描护照上传验证等。 具体的创建流程为： 输入出生日期。在创建儿童账户时，必须输入儿童的出生日期，这一日期将用于设置内容与媒体的筛选条件，以及家长控制的范围。 家长同意书并同意家庭隐私权声明。通过家长的 Apple 账户添加的付款方式，对家长身份进行验证，以确认家长是成年人。 设置儿童的 Apple 账户。使用电话号码或电子邮箱（必须项）为儿童创建 Apple 账户，即使使用电子邮箱创建也需要一个电话号码。通过该电话号码验证后，即可为儿童 Apple 账户设置密码。 在这里特别需要注意的是，建议大家使用电子邮箱为儿童创建 Apple 账户，创建完成后再完善添加电话号码。否则有可能触发神秘 bug，导致家长控制部分功能失效。 通过上述流程完成为儿童创建 Apple 账户，并加入家人共享，家长即可在自己的设备上看到家庭成员。 改进新儿童账户和家长控制的设置体验 在激活新设备时，家长可以直接在自己的 iPhone 上为儿童账户设置家长控制，确保儿童在通信、使用 App、浏览网页等行为上的安全。这样一来，家长可以在儿童第一次拿到 iPhone 或 iPad 时就建立好一套基础并完整的使用规则。 内容限制：儿童可以访问哪些内容？ 首先是内容限制。在这里，页面提供了一个年龄筛选器，用于筛选内容与服务的年龄等级。这些内容与服务包括网页内容、App、电影和电视节目、图书、Apple 媒体等。 这个年龄筛选器提供了从「4 岁及以下」 至 21 岁的选择范围，滑动它，下方的内容项目也会根据年龄筛选器，匹配不同过滤条件。例如，默认情况下，未满 18 周岁的儿童账户会启用「限制成人网站」，具体年龄规定可能因国家或地区而异；App 和电视节目的分级功能，也会自动适配年龄筛选器，以提供安全的内容保护。 内容限制可以在设备激活时设置，后期也可以在家长 iPhone 的家人共享里修改调整。 App 限制：选择儿童可以使用的原生 App 儿童帐户创建完成后，家长可以直接精确选择儿童在设备上可以访问的 App。Apple 还对设置流程进行了优化，以便于顺利地完成配置。 在初次配置儿童设备时，家长可以通过「设置助理」选择儿童在设备上可以访问的系统级 App，以便顺利完成设备的初始配置。 配置完成后，家长还可以在「App 与网站」中允许或阻止特定 App；「始终允许」则用于设置不受时间安排和时间限额影响的 App。 不被允许访问的 App 会在主屏幕中消失，但不会被删除。 儿童想要在 App Store 下载新的 App，也必须经得家长的同意，包括免费、付费 App 以及应用内购买。当然，删除 App 也可以设置为不允许儿童删除。这样，从激活新设备开始，一直到儿童长期的使用，家长对儿童可以使用的 App，都具有完整的控制权。 items.full_text_snippet: Matrix 首页推荐 Matrix 是少数派的写作社区，我们主张分享真实的产品体验，有实用价值的经验与思考。我们会不定期挑选 Matrix 最优质的文章，展示来自用户的最真实的体验和观点。 文章代表作者个人观点，少数派仅对标题和排版略作修改。 30年前的迷你笔记本电脑 1996年4月，东芝正式发布Libretto 20迷你笔记本电脑。从这时开始，越来越多的厂商在想「如何把一台完整的电脑做的越来越小，便于携带？」 图片来源： https://www.global.toshiba/ 而提到「把电脑做小」这件事，相信许多人和我一样，第一时间想到的是诸多经典的日系厂商曾经做过的产品。 本期《怀旧手记》就来聊聊早期的索尼是如何把电脑做的越来越小的？ 回到开篇我们提到的，在1996年东芝发布Libretto 20之后越来越多的日系厂商跟进「迷你笔记本电脑」这个概念。 索尼VAIO Picturebook 作为日系大厂的索尼自然也向大众展示了他们的答案：VAIO PCG-C1（Picturebook）。 图片来源： https://vaiolibrary.com/ 初代Picturebook 首款Picturebook发布于1998年9月，本身产量并不大，首批型号PCG-C1仅5000台。 作为迷你笔记本电脑，PCG-C1搭载Intel Pentium MMX 233MHz 处理器，并配备了当时极具创新性的可旋转内置摄像头。 电脑整机重量仅有约1公斤，并配备8.9英寸小尺寸屏幕，分辨率为1024x480。这是一块特殊的「超宽屏」长宽比约为 2.13:1，并非当时主流的4:3和我们现在熟知的16:9。 二代Picturebook 到了1999年，索尼顺势推出Picturebook的二代改版机型：PCG-C1X。 不同于初代小范围量产，二代Picturebook产量明显更多，并且除日本本土销售以外，还有对应的海外版本。配置方面，CPU是提升最大的，从初代的奔腾MMX，升级到奔腾II或赛扬。同时运存和存储也有进一步的提升。 我手上便有一台属于Picturebook二代当中的子型号机器：PCG-C1XA。 索尼VAIO PCG-C1XA 具体配置为： Intel Pentium II 400MHz 64MB RAM 12GB HDD 运行Windows98 Second Edition 虽然二代Picturebook在外观上相较于初代而言变化不大，但是还是有几个细微的升级：比如便于操控的Jog Dial（飞梭旋钮），以及双扬声器。 三代Picturebook 到了2000年9月，索尼发布了三代 Picturebook。 图片来源： https://vaiolibrary.com/ 三代Picturebook与全美达 和二代对比，外观变化虽然依旧不大，但是机器内部的核心硬件却经历了一次大换血——CPU 从英特尔彻底变成了全美达（Transmeta）。 图片来源： https://baike.baidu.com/ 至于为什么三代 Picturebook 的芯片会突然从英特尔变成全美达？我并没有找到索尼官方对此的明确解释，但如果我们结合当时的大环境，其实不难推测出原因。 在2000年前后，如果索尼想要给三代 C1 继续升级性能，英特尔阵营能选的升级方案主要是奔腾 III。但哪怕是专门给笔记本准备的奔腾 III-M，发热量和功耗依然不小。想要在一台只有 1kg 左右、内部空间紧凑到极点的迷你笔记本里塞进奔腾 III，要么散热压不住，要么电池续航直接崩掉，这在当时显然是不现实的。 而刚好在那个时间点，硅谷出现了一家红极一时的芯片初创公司——全美达（Transmeta）。他们主打的全美达 Crusoe 芯片，最大卖点就是低功耗、发热量小，而且续航比同时代采用英特尔芯片的机器要长得多。甚至连 Linux 之父 Linus Torvalds 当时都在这家公司任职，在当年可以说是赚足了眼球。 所以，追求极致轻薄和长续航的索尼，自然而然地把目光投向了全美达。不仅是索尼，当时很多的厂商在迷你笔记本当中，都不约而同地选择了全美达 Crusoe。不过，这次为了低功耗和续航做出的妥协，也为后来的实际体验埋下了不少伏笔。 同时除了全美达Crusoe，在三代高配版本的Picturebook当中还出现了内置Bluetooth，但是并没有内置WiFi。想要使用Picturebook上网，可以使用带无线网络功能的PCMCIA扩展卡或者使用有线上网、拨号上网。 四代Picturebook 在一年之后，2001年9月。索尼发布了Picturebook系列的最后一代。而第四代Picturebook在外观上终于跟前三代有所不同。 items.full_text_snippet: The EvalEval Coalition is thrilled to share that the UK AI Security Institute (AISI) is using EvalEval's infrastructure to openly share evaluation results, supporting more reproducible and verifiable evaluation science. AISI and EvalEval have previously collaborated on research that began at a joint workshop alongside NeurIPS 2025 , and feedback from the Institute has helped shape the Every Eval Ever (EEE) schema . This next phase of the collaboration puts that shared infrastructure into practice. Why reproducible evaluation reporting matters As AI deployment accelerates, evaluations are becoming increasingly important sources of evidence about model and system performance. Yet results are reported across many formats, platforms, and outlets, often without enough information to reproduce them. Running the evaluations again may itself be prohibitively expensive. EvalEval's mission is to improve this ecosystem through a shared reporting schema, Every Eval Ever , and an open platform, Evaluation Cards , that brings evaluation results and the information needed to interpret them into a common structure. This builds naturally on AISI's work to make evaluation more efficient through OptStop , more statistically rigorous through HiBayES , and more standardised in areas including transcript analysis and capability elicitation. Together, AISI and EvalEval are working to diagnose gaps in evaluation reporting and build shared infrastructure to close them. What AISI is sharing Transcript-level transparency matters not only for reproducibility, but also for analysis and diagnosis. In this new phase of the collaboration, AISI is making publicly reported evaluation methods and findings available through Evaluation Cards where appropriate. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 27 Oct 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 20 May 2026 (this version, v3)] Title: JanusCoder: Towards a Foundational Visual-Programmatic Interface for Code Intelligence View a PDF of the paper titled JanusCoder: Towards a Foundational Visual-Programmatic Interface for Code Intelligence, by Qiushi Sun and 8 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: The scope of neural code intelligence is rapidly expanding beyond text-based source code to encompass the rich visual outputs that programs generate. This visual dimension is critical for advanced applications like flexible content generation and precise, program-driven editing of visualizations. LLMs are automation rather than tools because they cannot be wielded. I agree
that outsourcing work can cost us opportunities to learn. But his conclusion
does not follow. Even by his definition, an LLM can be something a human wields.
And using it well takes skill, just as using other tools does. Picking up a saw does not guarantee a straight cut. Holding a chisel does not

division. Automation can be a feature of a tool. A compiler performs
substantial work without the programmer continuously directing each

items.full_text_snippet: Who is vfmaddrnd231pd?? October 12, 2026 vfmaddrnd231pd is a unique instruction from the FMA instruction set. Most instructions in that set have mnemonics like vfmadd231pd , but here rnd means something very specific. The Intel Software Development Manual documents it as: VFMADDRND231PD – Fused Multiply-Add of Packed Double-Precision Floating-Point Values with rounding control […] The immediate byte defines several bit fields that control rounding, DAZ, FTZ, and exception suppression (See Table 5-3). Most x86 floating-point instructions use the global rounding mode and settings, changing which is pretty slow. But vfmaddrnd231pd allows the rounding mode to be controlled on a per-instruction basis, and since FMA can emulate addition, subtraction, and multiplication, this mechanism effectively allows any arithmetic to have controllable rounding without AVX-512 – making some algorithms that rely on rounding incredibly faster. Or so it would , if this instruction actually existed. GNU assembler doesn’t recognize it. The Intel C/C++ Compiler intrinsics _mm_fmaddround_pd and _mm256_fmaddround_pd that SDM mentions are absent not only from Clang, but from ICC as well. This opcode is the only mention of DDS in the SDM, and this SO answer says that DDS is merely used for documentation and was removed from later SDM versions, but the fact that it’s still present here is suspicious. items.full_text_snippet: The original Amiga module I converted. A proper 1980s ear-worm! Of course, any good intro needs some music. On the Amiga, the standard was the “tracker” module format, which has a long and involved history of different forks, versions and tweaks. A song is built up from a series of patterns, each made up of rows of instructions. Each instruction usually includes note or pitch information, which sample to play and various parameters such as volume, effects - or in the case of some instructions, which position in the song to jump to. In many ways, it’s almost like a programming language for music. Using ProTracker as an example, a typical note cell is 4 bytes, shown on-screen as something like C-2 01 C20 . That breaks down into three fields: the note and octave ( C-2 ), the sample number ( 01 ), and the effect and its parameter ( C20 - in this case, “set the volume to $20 ”, which is half of the maximum $40 ). A close-up of Protracker playing a tune. Note the VUmeters - another classic demo effect I would pinch later on! For an impressive demonstration of what’s possible with a tracker and to see what the note data looks like on-screen, check out the work of h0ffman, and in particular his winning “ Professional Tracker ” entry from the Revision 2014 competition . He’s an undisputed master of the science (or art!) of tracking, and his “ Secrets of Protracker ” talk gives a great overview of what’s possible. The Amiga’s sound hardware far eclipsed anything else on the market at the time, and the ZX Spectrum is paltry by comparison. The original 48K models only offered a rudimentary “beeper”, but the later 128K models included a 3-channel AY-3-8912 sound chip. This was very popular in 8-bit micros of the time, and a more-or-less identical variant was also used in the Atari ST. items.full_text_snippet: Navigation Making big downloads resumable in firefox For whatever reason, Firefox 28 and newer (i.e. every modern version after like 2014 ) ships with network.http.response.timeout set to 300 seconds. This seems to interfere with resuming big downloads, as well as the general stability of big downloads. Setting network.http.response.timeout to 0 (or something very big) in about:config seems to make big downloads both resumable and at least a little more stable. I don't understand why this works, but experimental testing supports it. Note that this assumes the server supports resumable downloads; if it doesn't, no settings in firefox or any other browser are going to help. However, the problem this fixes is firefox being unable to resume a resumable download on error. I don't entirely know if this is the case, but it experimentally looks like resumable downloads in firefox rely on connection timeouts rather than the .part files they download. Firefox will happily ignore an existing .part without this option, and I do not understand why. Resumable downloads in firefox generally appear to be fairly unstable though. This has been a known problem in some form since as far back as 2005 . I also found that there's a manual .part shuffle to make firefox actually resume downloads , but I'm not doing that shit. As a non-firefox workaround, using wget -c -O "$filename" "$url" also works, and wget overall appears to be fairly stable. I do also suspect firefox does some hidden retries if it can before it considers the download to have failed - from some experimental testing, it does appear that this is at least partly related to network.http.response.timeout , and that exceeding the timeout interferes with this process. I have not attempted to confirm any of this with FF's source code, because I have no clue where to look.

projects.description: An open-source, clean-room reimplementation of Microsoft Word in pure Rust
projects.readme_excerpt:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft
cd wordcraft
cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- --sample        # the desktop app with the sample document
cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- report.docx     # open a document
```

Command line:

```sh
wordcraft-cli convert report.docx report.pdf        # docx, pdf, odt, rtf, html, md, tex, txt, png
wordcraft-cli text report.docx                      # plain text
wordcraft-cli inspect report.docx                   # structure as JSON
wordcraft-cli run --template sample \
  --cmd 'select.text={"text":"Membership"}' --cmd format.bold --save out.docx
```

Web: `cd apps/wordcraft-web && trunk serve`, then open <http://127.0.0.1:8771/?sample>.
projects.readme_intro: WordCraft Writing and document design; an open-source, clean-room reimplementation of Microsoft Word, rebuilt in pure Rust. A fast, open-source word processor with the Word workflow you already know: the ribbon, styles, tables, track changes, references and mail merge. It reads and writes .docx, runs natively on macOS, Windows, Linux and BSD, and in the browser via WebAssembly. By the ArtCraft team.
